details.description: Nova-3 General is the default, general-purpose option in Deepgram's Nova-3 speech-to-text family, documented as "optimized for everyday audio processing" and recommended for meetings, event captioning, multi-speaker, multilingual, noisy, or far-field audio in both batch and streaming. Deepgram's docs list it under the same language-support table row as the bare `nova-3` model id, meaning calling the API with `model=nova-3` uses this same general option. Deepgram also offers nova-3-medical and nova-3-pharma variants, tuned for healthcare and pharmaceutical vocabulary, as separate Nova-3 options.
advantages: Deepgram reports a 53.4% reduction in word error rate for real-time streaming and a 47.4% reduction for batch transcription compared to the competitors it tested, per its documentation.
Supports real-time multilingual transcription with code-switching across English, Spanish, French, German, Hindi, Russian, Portuguese, Japanese, Italian, and Dutch within a single conversation.
Deepgram describes it as the first of its voice AI models to offer self-serve vocabulary customization, letting users adapt to new terms without retraining the model.
Includes an optional personal-information redaction feature, per Deepgram's documentation.
disadvantages: Not tuned for medical or pharmaceutical vocabulary; Deepgram offers separate nova-3-medical and nova-3-pharma variants for those domains.
use_cases: General-purpose transcription of meetings, events, and multi-speaker conversations in noisy or far-field conditions.
Real-time multilingual transcription with code-switching for customer support or contact-center audio.
Batch transcription of recorded audio that needs custom vocabulary adapted without retraining.

sources.title: Introducing Nova-3: Setting a New Standard for AI-Driven Speech-to-Text

notes: developers.deepgram.com/docs/model documents model=nova-3-{option} with general/medical/pharma as the only listed options ('general: Optimized for everyday audio processing'), and models-languages-overview lists `nova-3` and `nova-3-general` together in the same language-support table row, so this entry treats nova-3-general and the bare nova-3 id as the same model. The current docs/model page states a 53.4%/47.4% WER reduction; Deepgram's original October 2024 launch post (introducing-nova-3-speech-to-text-api) instead states 54.2% streaming / 47.4% batch with median WERs of 6.84% and 5.26%, and the also-current models-languages-overview page still shows that same older 54.2% figure too -- docs/model (the dedicated model-options page) is treated as the more authoritative, updated number, so 53.4% is the one used here. WER figures are not included in evaluations since they are not accuracy-style, higher-is-better scores. Only the 10 languages named above support real-time code-switching; the rest are single-language support.
